sources.note: Company overview. Four market segments (providers, life sciences, payers, health IT vendors). Products listed but no mention of 'Veradigm View' by name — only 'Practice Fusion EHR' and 'Veradigm EHR'.
ONC mandatory disclosures page. Lists 5 certified products including 'Veradigm View.' EHI export documentation links (V1-V6). MFA and cost documentation.

EHR solutions page. Two EHRs: Veradigm EHR (advanced, multi-specialty) and Practice Fusion EHR (simple, independent practices). No mention of 'Veradigm View' confirming it is the certification name for Practice Fusion.
Practice Fusion product page. Returned 403 at time of research. Content described elsewhere as positioning Practice Fusion for small/independent practices with cloud-based, no-IT-needed approach.
EHI export documentation V5 for Veradigm View. Lists 70+ data tables across 7 categories. Internally references 'Practice Fusion EHR' in entity descriptions.
Veradigm solution login page. Lists Practice Fusion login, FollowMyHealth, ePrescribe, etc. No 'Veradigm View' login — further confirms View = Practice Fusion.
Veradigm View EHR Login page. Confirms it is a full EHR system with dedicated domain veradigmview.com.
Veradigm View Customer Community / help site. Separate from main Veradigm support infrastructure.
Company overview. Founded 1986, 'integrated data systems and services company.' No mention of Veradigm View.
Definitive Healthcare market share data. Veradigm holds ~3.1% (7th place) with 2,580 installations in ambulatory EHR market.

Capterra reviews for Practice Fusion. 3.7/5 rating from 429 reviews. Users praise ease of use and affordability; criticize limited customization and inconsistent support. Used by small to medium practices.

EMRSystems 2024 review of Practice Fusion. Describes customizable templates, e-prescribing, billing/claims management, patient portal, telemedicine, analytics. Targets small to medium practices prioritizing affordability.
Corporate history timeline for Veradigm/Allscripts. Key acquisitions including Practice Fusion (2018, $100M), divestiture of hospital segment to Altera (2022), rebrand to Veradigm (2023).
Veradigm FHIR API documentation. References 'Veradigm EHR' as primary product; does not mention Veradigm View, suggesting separate API infrastructure.
